points.description: States that corner (interest point) information improves image segmentation (Harris corner detection used for this).
points.partial_credit: Half only if segmentation is named but the role of corners is vague.

points.description: States that corners allow edges to be detected more efficiently (edge detection).
points.partial_credit: Half only if edges are mentioned without the corner link stated clearly.

points.description: States that corner details improve object classification/recognition.
points.partial_credit: Half only if object recognition is named without stating corners improve it.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three applications stated precisely as benefiting from corners: image segmentation, edge detection, and object classification. Generic statements like "used in computer vision" earn nothing. A wrong application listed alongside costs that point; final total is rounded to a whole mark 0, 1 or 2 (all three = 2, two = 1, fewer = 0 or as sums dictate).
